**Instructions.** Choose the single best answer (a–e) for each question. You may use a periodic table.
Calculators are allowed. Answers are rounded to the precision shown. Time yourself: aim for about 30 minutes
(roughly 2 minutes per question, the same pace as the full exam). **Solubility rules are not provided:** work from memory, as on the exam.

**Answer sheet.** Use the bubble answer sheet (`CHEM1301/exam-prep/answer-sheet/answer-sheet.pdf`), rows 1–15.

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**1.** What is the name for a reaction in aqueous solution that results in the formation of a solid?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ A precipitation reaction\
b)\ A decomposition reaction\
c)\ An oxidation–reduction reaction\
d)\ A neutralization (acid–base) reaction\
e)\ A combustion reaction

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

\needspace{9\baselineskip}

**5.** Aqueous solutions of Mg(NO~3~)~2~ and KOH are mixed. What is the **net ionic** equation?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ K^+^(aq) + NO~3~^−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ KNO~3~(s)\
b)\ Mg^2+^(aq) + OH^−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ Mg(OH)~2~(s)\
c)\ No reaction occurs (NR)\
d)\ Mg^2+^(aq) + 2NO~3~^−^(aq) + 2K^+^(aq) + 2OH^−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ Mg(OH)~2~(s) + 2K^+^(aq) + 2NO~3~^−^(aq)\
e)\ Mg^2+^(aq) + 2OH^−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ Mg(OH)~2~(s)

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```

**9.** Which is the balanced **molecular** equation for mixing aqueous Ni(NO~3~)~2~ and Na~3~PO~4~?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ Ni(NO~3~)~2~(aq) + Na~3~PO~4~(aq) $\rightarrow$ Ni~3~(PO~4~)~2~(s) + NaNO~3~(aq)\
b)\ Ni(NO~3~)~2~(aq) + Na~3~PO~4~(aq) $\rightarrow$ NiPO~4~(s) + NaNO~3~(aq)\
c)\ 3Ni(NO~3~)~2~(aq) + 2Na~3~PO~4~(aq) $\rightarrow$ Ni~3~(PO~4~)~2~(s) + 6NaNO~3~(aq)\
d)\ 3Ni(NO~3~)~2~(aq) + 2Na~3~PO~4~(aq) $\rightarrow$ Ni~3~(PO~4~)~2~(aq) + 6NaNO~3~(s)\
e)\ No reaction (NR)

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```

**12.** Aqueous solutions of mercury(I) nitrate and potassium chloride are mixed. What is the **net ionic** equation?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ Hg~2~^2+^(aq) + 2Cl^−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ Hg~2~Cl~2~(s)\
b)\ Hg~2~^2+^(aq) + 2NO~3~^−^(aq) + 2K^+^(aq) + 2Cl^−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ Hg~2~Cl~2~(s) + 2K^+^(aq) + 2NO~3~^−^(aq)\
c)\ K^+^(aq) + NO~3~^−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ KNO~3~(s)\
d)\ No reaction occurs (NR)\
e)\ Hg~2~^2+^(aq) + Cl^−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ Hg~2~Cl~2~(s)

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

**15.** When aqueous KNO~3~ and NaCl are mixed, no reaction occurs. Which statement explains why?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ Ions with the same charge can't react with each other\
b)\ A precipitate forms, but it redissolves immediately\
c)\ Nitrate ions always react to form a gas\
d)\ Both possible products are soluble, so no solid forms and the ions simply stay dissolved\
e)\ KNO~3~ and NaCl are both insoluble, so they can't react

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```
